criterion: RT stage R1: every run of the rasterizer checks, failures included (bounds: evidence/rt-r1-bounds.json, committed e9351b1 before any run)

runs.result: fail: C1 on tie_grid_jittered, 3 double hits; every other C1 mesh, C2 and C3 within bounds, every control failing as required
runs.diagnosis: The jittered grid moved inner vertices up to 3 px on a 9 px grid. An independent Python mirror of the generator found one triangle (cell 9, 18) wound opposite to the other 1,151: the quad folded, so the input was not a planar triangulation and any fill rule covers its neighbours twice. The fault is the test mesh, not the rasterizer.
runs.change: Jitter reduced to 2 px on each axis (the mirror's smallest doubled area is then 1,390,886 fixed-point units, positive). A precondition check was added: every input triangle of a C1 mesh must have the same winding; on the 3 px mesh it reports 1 folded triangle. The bound is unchanged.

runs.backend: D3D12 on the RTX 4090 (driver 610.88), under D:/gpu.lock.d, binaries at 5d00b3f
runs.result: fail on the RTX: C4 passes on every case but one, clip_stress affine (1 pixel's UV at 1.14x the bound); C5 fails on every scene: 335 of 635 (retro_room), 518 of 1,436 (iso_street) and 10 of 23 (clip_stress) valid slots differ from the CPU's (bound 1%); coordinates stay within one grid step except 8 on clip_stress; pixel triangle ids agree or are explained by a differing slot on every pixel; clip_stress also exceeds the depth bound (13,303 pixels over 1e-6, worst 8.3e-6) and, in affine and whole-pixel modes, the UV bound (worst 59x and 122x). Controls fail as required (14,831; 1; 2).
runs.diagnosis: Inferred, not yet confirmed: D3D12 allows fp32 division to be approximate (2.5 ulp) and the NVIDIA driver compiles 1/w and the affine w/sum that way, while WARP and SwiftShader divide exactly. 1/w feeds every snapped coordinate and every z, which explains near-tie snaps one unit apart and the depth drift; on clip_stress the UVs reach 300, so a 2-ulp weight error is large in UV. A follow-up would move the reciprocals to the host-side setup data or test a correctly rounded division; the bounds stay as committed.
